scope: Final source review and independent verification of existing owner raw test logs and recorded project inputs; no test, service, benchmark, or performance execution by reviewer.
test_input_binding: Before/after recorded tracked platform/controller project files plus read_page_v1_golden.json equal each other, current actual bytes, and all Git blobs at the exact commit. This is the recorded project input scope, not a claim to inventory every host/toolchain runtime file.
boundary_findings: Text and integer-lexeme UTF8 gates both route invalid sequences to the entire original row path. ASCII controls, HTML, quote/backslash, U+2028/U+2029 and valid UTF8 boundaries have exact standard Encoder byte oracles; valid cases assert fast support so all-fallback cannot pass.

Float parse and spelling stay with json.Number.Float64 then standard json.Marshal; threshold/negative-zero/subnormal/extreme and fixed-seed random finite-bit cases compare old encoding. Integer lexemes retain string semantics including empty, +1, 01 and values beyond i64.
Whole-row prepare only creates immutable owned descriptions and float bytes. Tests assert no header, writes, row-buffer, or error changes, and late unsupported cells publish nothing.
Two prepared closures interleave and repeat after caller row mutation; exact bytes remain owned and correct.

Raw and generic entry share sticky Write errors. Both directions, zero/partial/full error and nil short writes are compared against the same standard Encoder oracle, including accepted prefixes and attempted full bytes.
Generic Marshal errors remain nonsticky; later valid raw writes succeed. Prior raw Write error suppresses MarshalJSON side effects and preserves the first error.

Each supported row performs one complete line-plus-LF Write. Large rows remain accepted; retained row capacity is at most64KiB and small-row reuse resumes after a large row. This is not a cap on transient or total process memory.
preserved_boundaries: Only JSON output construction/serialization changes; protobuf methods unchanged.
Shared cursor executor differs only in JSON constructor invocation; no SQL, audit, cancellation, fencing, quota, page Flush or cleanup order change.
Old all-byte test remains and compares fallback bytes; old unsupported, late-invalid-value, audited dispatch and existing response/cursor tests are retained.
limits: No performance gain or business p99 claim from source correctness and test PASS.
UTF8 validation plus byte scan adds a two-pass tradeoff; real workload gate remains required.
Static and differential tests do not prove all possible inputs; randomized cases are deterministic fixed seeds.
Network atomicity is not claimed; each row is prepared before its single Write, and old short-write behavior is deliberately retained.
New standalone build provenance is owned separately by optimization_council and is not substituted for these test bindings.
